confirmed.title: Advanced/expert group vote cannot be completed as instructed: partial votes strand the verdict, toggling flashes a false 'Correct' verdict with win cue, and a live Next silently forfeits a correctly placed card
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1&seed=33003 as a fresh visitor (clear localStorage)
New game -> Skip photo x4 -> Advanced -> First to 5 -> Shuffle & start -> continue the pass screen -> tap the vinyl to draw
Place in a CORRECT gap for the card's year (read __timeline.state to pick it) -> Place here

Scenario: player named the title but NOT the artist. Per the panel copy 'Group votes — tap what they got right', tap Title only — the banner stays 'Waiting for the group — vote Title and Artist to settle it.' indefinitely; there is no control that records a No

Exit A: wait ~800ms past the tap guard and tap Next player once — the app advances to the pass screen and the correctly placed card is silently discarded with no verdict, sound, or message (standings unchanged)

Exit B: instead tap Artist ON — a full false green 'Correct. The card is yours.' renders with seat-pill bump, leader crown and win cue — then tap Artist OFF: the verdict flips to red 'Right spot, but you had to name it too.', and the recorded No renders identically to never-voted (aria-pressed=false, dashed outline)
confirmed.expected: The group can record 'they got it wrong' as instructed; no verdict, win cue, or scoreboard change renders until the vote settles; Next is blocked (or clearly announces the forfeit) while the vote is open.
confirmed.actual: The confirmations model is tri-state with no direct path to No: a single tap leaves the other field null so the verdict strands at 'Waiting'; tapping a chip ON makes both fields non-null and immediately renders acceptance (false 'Correct' banner + win sfx) until the OFF tap corrects it; btn-next-player is never disabled while the vote is open, so tapping it resolves nulls as unconfirmed and silently discards the correctly placed card.

confirmed.title: 'Play again' clears the finished game's saved result at tap time, so a reload during post-game setup permanently loses the winner screen and payout QR while the pot may still be unsettled
repro: Fresh page at https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1&seed=42424: New game; Skip photo on all rows; First to 5; Buy-in ON; enter a Venmo handle; Shuffle & start
Play to the win screen (it shows THE POT $8, Send it to @handle, and the payout QR)
Tap 'Play again — same players' (lands on the setup screen)
Reload the page — exactly what switching to the Venmo app and back does on most phones
Land on home: no 'See final result' card, no resume — the saved game key and the buy-in snapshot were removed at Play-again tap time, before any new game started
confirmed.expected: The finished game's recap and pot stay reachable until a NEW game actually starts — the app's own persist() rationale is that finished games are saved precisely because switching to Venmo to settle reloads the tab.
confirmed.actual: The play-again handler runs state=null; clearGame(); removeStored(ACTIVE_BUYIN_KEY) immediately on tap and only then shows setup; any reload from the setup screen lands on a bare home with winner, pot amount, and payout QR permanently gone.
sources: persistence:"Play again" instantly destroys the finished game's saved result, so a reload during post-game setup loses the winner screen and payout QR while the pot may still be unsettled
confirmed.rationale: Raised from the reporter's S3 to S2: the app's own designed guarantee (finished game reachable after the switch-to-Venmo reload, stated in the code comment) breaks in exactly its target scenario, destroying the settlement record and QR mid-settlement — that is a broken feature / 'resume misses', the rubric's S2. Not S1 data loss: the clear is user-initiated ('Play again'), no live game or roster vanishes (the players draft survives into setup), money math is untouched (buy-in is deeplink-only), and the humans still know who won. I confirmed the immediate clear is still present at HEAD in the 'play-again' action handler.

confirmed.title: First tap on an enabled 'Played before' guest chip does nothing when focus is still in a name field
repro: Fresh visitor: New game, reduce to two rows named Ana and Bob, give Ana a photo via her row's picker, Skip photo for Bob, Shuffle & start (this seeds the guest list)
Menu -> Home -> New game (the Ana/Bob draft restores; both guest chips show greyed 'already playing')
Tap into Ana's name field and type a different name (e.g. 'Zed'), leaving focus in the field — Ana's chip un-greys
Immediately tap the enabled Ana chip once
confirmed.expected: One tap seats Ana as a new player row with her saved photo, and the chip greys back to 'already playing'.
confirmed.actual: The first tap does nothing — no row added, no announcement, chip stays enabled; a second tap (or blurring the field first) seats her normally. Mechanism: leaving the field fires the change-commit which rebuilds the chip list mid-tap, so the click lands on a detached node.
sources: roster:First tap on a 'Played before' chip does nothing when it follows typing in a name field
confirmed.rationale: S3 as reported: a deterministic silently-eaten first tap on the natural type-then-tap party flow is 'janky-but-recoverable' — the immediate second tap works and nothing dead-ends, so it does not reach S2's broken-feature bar. The reporter supplies a credible mechanism (chip list rebuilt on blur) and a control variant proving it, so it is a strong pass-through to verification.

v1.reason: Ran the exact repro twice in fresh Chrome sessions (Playwright UI-only, live Vercel site) via scratch/qa/round-3/verify-guest-chip-first-tap-swallowed-1/verify.mjs. Both runs: after seeding Ana(photo)/Bob(skip), re-entering New game, renaming Ana's row to Zed with focus left in the field, the un-greyed Ana chip ignored the first tap (rows stayed [Zed, Bob], chip stayed enabled, no announcement); the second tap seated Ana with her saved photo and re-greyed the chip. A passive capture-phase event log proves the mechanism: first tap dispatched mousedown+mouseup but NO click event — the blur-commit change handler runs paintPeople() whose replaceChildren detaches the chip mid-tap, so Chrome suppresses the click and the document-delegated onClick never fires (matches ui.js source: onInput 'change' branch → paintPeople). Control variant confirmed: blur first, then one tap seats Bob immediately, isolating focus-in-field as the trigger. Only deviation from the written steps: reaching the menu required tapping through the pass screen (#btn-pass-continue) since it has no menu button — not material. Zero page/console errors. Severity S3 per rubric: janky-but-recoverable (immediate second tap works, nothing dead-ends), below S2's broken-feature bar, above S4 polish. Evidence: verify.mjs, run-2.log, screenshots 00-05 in the verify directory.
